headlines.title: What the Coming 6G Trials With Nvidia, T-Mobile Could Mean for Nokia Investors
headlines.summary: Nokia stock has surged nearly 150% over the past year on the promise of AI-powered 6G, and now Nvidia and T-Mobile are putting that promise to a real-world test. What the trial results could mean for shareholders depends on a question Nokia has not yet answered.

headlines.title: T-Mobile excludes 2 generous customer perks from new phone plans
headlines.summary: T-Mobile made a significant change last week by rolling out new wireless plans under its new “Nothing” initiative to attract price-conscious customers. However, its new offerings lack two generous customer perks that were once included in a few of its plans.

headlines.title: T-Mobile's CEO just dismantled SpaceX and Starlink's big goal
headlines.summary: SpaceX's first earnings call put the wireless industry on notice. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and COO Gwynne Shotwell said Starlink was coming for Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile. They cited a $600 billion U.S. wireless market and said they expected to take customers from all three.

headlines.title: T Mobile US (TMUS) Could Be 27% Undervalued On New Plan Rollout
headlines.summary: T-Mobile US (TMUS) has introduced a new suite of plans built around longer term device financing and student focused discounts, prompting fresh attention on how the stock reflects its current pricing strategy. See our latest analysis for T-Mobile US. For investors watching T-Mobile US, the recent plan refresh comes after a period where the share price has eased, with a 30 day share price return of 4.81% and a year to date share price return of 10.52% in decline.

headlines.title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: SpaceX, Meta, Palantir, Snowflake, Alphabet, AT&T and T-Mobile
headlines.summary: SpaceX's AI compute and Starlink businesses are surging, while Starship advances and CAPEX normalization could fuel its next phase of growth.

description: T-Mobile US, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides wireless communications services in the United States, Puerto Rico, and the United States Virgin Islands. The company offers voice, messaging, and data services to postpaid, prepaid, and wholesale and other services customers. It also provides wireless devices, including smartphones, wearables, tablets, home broadband gateways, headsets, and other mobile communication devices, as well as accessories; financing through equipment installment plans; reinsurance for device insurance policies and extended warranty contracts. The company offers services under the T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile brands through its owned and operated retail stores, customer care channels, national retailers, and its websites, as well as through T-Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile, and Mint Mobile apps. It also sells devices to dealers and other third-party distributors for resale through independent third-party retail outlets and various third-party websites. It has 700 MHz wireless spectrum licenses. The company was founded in 1994 and is headquartered in Bellevue, Washington. T-Mobile US, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of Deutsche Telekom AG.
